newsitem.title: CHINA: China's economy seen overtaking 1996 target.
newsitem.headline: China's economy seen overtaking 1996 target.

text.p: China's economy grew an estimated 9.7 percent in 1996, outstripping a government target of 8.0 percent aimed at cooling economic growth, officials said on Monday.
They forecast 10.5 percent expansion next year.
Gross domestic product was estimated at 6.780 trillion yuan ($816 billion) in 1996, according to provisional figures issued by the State Statistical Bureau.
China had set a target of 8.0 percent growth for 1996 to try to cool the economy, down from 10.2 percent last year and a sizzling 11.8 percent the previous year.

Retail price inflation, China's benchmark price figure, was estimated to have risen by about 6.0 percent year-on-year, down from 14.8 percent in 1995. The 1996 figure was well below a government target of 10 percent and lower than the economic growth rate, the bureau said.
Consumer price inflation was estimated at about 8.3 percent, compared with 17.1 percent in 1995.
The government has set reining in inflation as its prime target after the retail price index raced to a communist-era high of 21.4 percent in 1994.
Fixed asset investment in 1996 was estimated to have grown 18.9 percent in 1996, or 12.5 percent after adjusting for inflation, to 2.380 trillion yuan, the bureau said.

Industrial output was estimated to have grown by 13 percent in 1996, down by about one percentage point, the bureau said. Earlier figures said industrial output growth for 1995 was 13.4 percent and it was not clear if that had been adjusted.
China's trade surplus was provisionally estimated at about $16 billion this year, compared with the $16.7 billion surplus reported for 1995.
Exports recovered in the second half of the year after slumping in the first half, spurred by faster repayment of export tax rebates to exporters, the bureau said.

Total trade was estimated at $290 billion in 1996, up by 3.3 percent compared with last year. Of that, exports were estimated to have risen by about 3.0 percent to $153 billion while imports rose about 4.0 percent to $137 billion yuan, the bureau said.
Actual foreign investment for 1996 was estimated at $48 billion, rising by about 7.0 percent, it said.
The bureau estimated a record grain harvest of 480 million tonnes for 1996, up from a previous record of 466 million tonnes last year.

However, output of cotton in 1996 was estimated at 4.0 million tonnes, down by 800,000 tonnes from last year. Earlier estimates had placed the 1995 crop at about 4.4 million tonnes and it was unclear if that figure had been revised.
The bureau estimated total output of oil-bearing crops at 21.9 million tonnes, falling by 600,000 tonnes from last year.
It estimated per capita income of urban residents at 4,380 yuan, rising by an inflation-adjusted 3.4 percent, but said many low-income families were suffering difficulties.
The per capita incomes of rural residents grew faster, by about 8.0 percent in real terms, to 1,900 yuan. ($1 = 8.3 yuan)
